title: Choose how the landing page unfolds below the street
question: The world is settled (the photographed lane, lit night, serial lights). This round picks the page's structure. The roll leads with the scroll-lit lane. None of the six catalog challengers (BBS, nixie counter, brick manual, silk canopy, Massin stage, magazine program) beat these on audience fit or clarity, so none earned a card.

options.label: Lights on, street by street
options.lineage: The baked light groups of the hero, driven by scroll instead of a clock
options.thesis: Scrolling switches the street on: the page's progress is the plan's progress, bulbs coming on group by group.
options.viewport: Below the hero the lane pins and goes dark. Three chapters scroll over it (Describe, Plan by function, Celebrate together); each one switches on another light group in the photo, and the last lights everything. A real product preview rides in smoked glass beside each chapter.
options.risk: A pinned section is a long scroll on phones; the chapters must stay short and the pin must release cleanly.

options.label: One evening, start to finish
options.lineage: A wedding run sheet, the product's own timeline output
options.thesis: The page is one celebration evening told as a run sheet: 4 pm haldi to 11 pm reception, each time stamp a section with its own rendered scene.
options.viewport: A vertical time rail runs down the left edge with glowing time stamps. Each stamp opens a full-bleed rendered scene (haldi courtyard, mehendi, sangeet stage, mandap) with the matching slice of a real plan in glass beside it.
options.risk: Needs four or five more Blender scenes; wedding-heavy, so birthdays and community events must appear in the close.

options.label: The family thread
options.lineage: How Indian families actually plan: a group chat with everyone in it
options.thesis: The page is the family group conversation where the plan gets made: relatives ask, Subham answers with a plan card, and changes wait for approval.
options.viewport: Over a darkened slice of the lane, a wide conversation column builds as you scroll: Amma asks about the budget in Tamil, a cousin asks about Mehendi, and Subham answers each with a live plan card and an Approve button.
options.risk: Chat can read as a messaging-app costume; it must stay generic and never imitate WhatsApp's look.
